labels.name: Segmentation
labels.definition: Divide an object, system, process, or responsibility into independent or differently managed parts so the desired improvement becomes possible.
positive_examples: Divide one long processing line into independently controlled short zones.
near_misses: Removing one component entirely is Taking Out unless independent parts are central to the solution.

labels.name: Inversion
labels.definition: Reverse an action, arrangement, sequence, direction, role, or operating condition so the desired improvement becomes possible.
positive_examples: Reverse the order of two operations so the fragile step occurs after stabilization.
near_misses: Waiting for a sensor signal is Feedback or gating unless the operative order or condition is actually reversed.

labels.name: Both
labels.definition: Use both segmentation and inversion as essential parts of the same stated solution.
positive_examples: Split a workflow into independent stages and reverse the order of two stages to resolve the contradiction.
near_misses: Choose the single dominant operator when the second operator is merely incidental wording.

labels.name: Other
labels.definition: The transformation is clear but its dominant operator is neither Segmentation nor Inversion.
positive_examples: Continuously adapt a component shape to conditions, which is better classified as Dynamics.
near_misses: Use Cannot determine rather than Other when the displayed information is insufficient to identify any operator.

abstention.name: Cannot determine
abstention.definition: The displayed information is insufficient, ambiguous, or internally inconsistent, so no reliable operator classification can be made.

decision_rule: Classify the dominant operator in the stated transformation, not the domain or isolated vocabulary. Use Both only when both operators are essential. Use Other when another operator is identifiable. Use Cannot determine when the evidence is insufficient. Record a rationale and score operator presence, essentiality, contradiction resolution, and feasibility independently.

ordinal_dimensions.name: Operator presence
ordinal_dimensions.definition: How clearly the selected operator is present in the stated transformation.

ordinal_dimensions.name: Operator essentiality
ordinal_dimensions.definition: How necessary the selected operator is to the stated solution.

ordinal_dimensions.name: Contradiction resolution
ordinal_dimensions.definition: How completely the stated transformation resolves the described contradiction.

ordinal_dimensions.name: Solution feasibility
ordinal_dimensions.definition: How plausible the stated solution is under the displayed constraints.

agreement_policy.adjudication_rule: Case-level unanimity on a substantive label required for freeze; disagreements and unanimous abstentions remain explicit for adjudication.
